solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Having been elected, a Conservative has to make rude gesture very rarely

parts.note: something that has been in the past was once so
a party elected is in, in power
blue is the colour of the UK Conservative Party, so a Tory is a blue
to moon is to bare one's backside as an insult

explanation.surface: A politician, newly voted in, behaves so badly that he flashes his backside at someone, though only on the rarest of occasions.
explanation.walkthrough: BLUE for Conservative relies on the party's colour in Britain; to MOON is to show one's bare bottom as a gesture of contempt.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: a blue moon is a rare second full moon in a month, so the phrase means hardly ever.

clue.text: It rarely produces something of value in solver's world, perhaps

definitions.text: It rarely produces something of value
definitions.meaning: a shellfish that only occasionally yields a pearl
from the saying that the world is your shellfish, i.e. yours for the taking; the solver is 'you'

explanation.surface: A wry remark about something that seldom pays off in the crossword solver's universe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solver's' stands for 'your': the saying is 'the world is your oyster'.
explanation.definitionFit: The bivalve occasionally contains a pearl, and the proverb makes it the world laid open to you.

clue.text: One conducting hostile takeover perhaps seizes account, one that'll take charge?

indicators.note: the takeover merchant grabs and holds the following pieces inside himself

parts.note: a captor seizes something by force, a hostile takeover being one example
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A corporate raider grabs a client's account, and asks whether this is someone who will take charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take charge' reads as leadership but means storing electric charge.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrical component that stores electric charge between two plates, so it literally holds charge.

clue.text: Press office kicking off about useful stuff that's dug up

parts.note: to press clothes is to iron them

indicators.note: the start of the word office is what is wanted, its opening letter

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A press office starts briefing about something useful that has been unearthed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' is a verb for smoothing clothes, not the media.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock mined for its metal content is valuable material extracted from the ground.

clue.text: Australian's desire to have letter dropped off in Wapping?

parts.note: an itch is a restless craving

explanation.surface: An Australian longs to have a letter delivered by being dropped off in an East London district.
explanation.walkthrough: Wapping is in East London, where Cockney speakers drop the letter H ('Wapping' becomes ''Wapping', 'Ackney' for Hackney).
explanation.definitionFit: The name of the eighth letter of the alphabet, which Cockney speech famously leaves unsounded.

clue.text: Pound continually advanced, financed by borrowing

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound (libra)
ever means always or continually
advanced in years means aged

explanation.surface: Sterling kept rising, funded by loans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'advanced' looks financial but means old.
explanation.definitionFit: A leveraged company or deal is funded largely with debt rather than equity.

clue.text: Painter with broken leg to paint again after losing a little time

indicators.note: a broken leg is in pieces, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the repainting word drops a letter, standing for time

parts.note: to recoat is to apply another coat of paint
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A decorator with a broken leg has to repaint, having wasted a bit of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' makes ELG from LEG; 'after losing' takes A and T from RECOAT, leaving RECO, which follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cretan-born artist who worked in Toledo is a celebrated Spanish Renaissance painter.

clue.text: Visual form's no go

parts.note: O is a zero, nothing
to part is to go away or depart

explanation.surface: A curt verdict that some visual form is off limits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no go' reads as a single phrase meaning forbidden; split it into nothing and depart.
explanation.definitionFit: A 1960s style of abstract painting using optical illusions is a form of visual art.

clue.text: Win-win outcome for those making money

parts.note: to net something is to win it
to gain is to win

explanation.surface: A deal where everyone benefits, described from the point of view of the profit-makers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Win-win' is split into its two halves, each a verb meaning obtain.
explanation.definitionFit: Profit after deductions is the overall increase that moneymakers end up with.

clue.text: Fans drink wine

parts.note: to sup is to drink
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Supporters drink wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A team's followers are collectively its backing, the crowd behind it.

clue.text: Homeless veteran's first to get an allowance

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word veteran is taken

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, a
a grant is a sum allowed or awarded

explanation.surface: A homeless former soldier is the first in line to receive financial help.
explanation.definitionFit: A drifter has no fixed home and wanders from place to place.

clue.text: Flying ace and sexy female — you and me?

indicators.note: letters in flight are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
hot means sexy
her is a female pronoun

explanation.surface: A pilot ace and an attractive woman make a couple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flying' suggests an air ace, but it rearranges ACE to EAC.
explanation.definitionFit: A reciprocal pronoun phrase: two people, such as you and me, relate to one another.

clue.text: Bolt-on unlimited texts half price

indicators.note: without its limits, the word texts loses its first and last letters
only the first half of the word for a price is used

parts.note: a rate is a price or charge

explanation.surface: An add-on deal offering unlimited texts at half price, like a mobile phone package.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unlimited' sounds like a phone tariff but strips TEXTS to EXT; 'half' takes RA from RATE.
explanation.definitionFit: An add-on is something additional attached to a basic product or service.

clue.text: Influencing op-ed feature through which bias to left or right is controlled?

definitions.text: through which bias to left or right is controlled?

parts.note: steering means guiding or influencing
a newspaper column appears on the opinion page

explanation.surface: Talk of political spin: an opinion piece that shapes the paper's leftward or rightward slant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bias to left or right' sounds political but refers to a car pulling to one side.
explanation.definitionFit: The shaft carrying a car's wheel lets the driver correct any drift to either side.

clue.text: Rain splashed on butts behind

indicators.note: splashed rain is scattered, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
rears are backsides or butts

explanation.surface: Rain spattering onto people's backsides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'splashed' makes INAR from RAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Behind with payments or work is the idiomatic sense of being late on what is owed.

clue.text: Annual rut bucks staged

indicators.note: bucking is jumping about wildly, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: In the yearly mating season, male deer put on a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bucks' looks like male deer in the rut but is a verb signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Something staged is contrived or artificial, not spontaneous or natural.

clue.text: Slip during PE — danger in loose seat fixing

indicators.note: the slip happens in the middle of PE, so it goes inside

parts.note: physical education is done in the gym
to err is to make a slip

indicators.note: letters let loose are freed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A slip in a gym class causes danger from a loose seat that needs fixing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' makes ANDERING from DANGER IN. 'seat' means an electoral constituency.
explanation.definitionFit: Manipulating constituency boundaries rigs electoral seats in a party's favour.

clue.text: Region of northwest Spanish city

definitions.meaning: the name of the ITV franchise covering northwest England, so its area was known by it
the Andalusian city home of the Alhambra

explanation.surface: A geography question about a city in northwest Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: Granada Television was the ITV (British commercial TV) company for northwest England, so its broadcast area was called the Granada region. The Spanish city is in the south, not the northwest.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share the name: a British television area and a city in Andalusia.

clue.text: Gave up as flickering eyelid finally closed

indicators.note: a flickering eyelid moves about, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the final letter of closed is taken

explanation.surface: Someone surrendered as their fluttering eyelid at last shut.
explanation.definitionFit: To surrender or concede is to give way, give in, relinquish.

clue.text: Is rough crook like this?

indicators.note: crook as an adjective means bent or out of shape, so these letters are bent into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A question whether a tough criminal fits this description.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crook' looks like a criminal noun but works as the rearrangement signal, while the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough villain would naturally be described as rascally, behaving like a scoundrel.

clue.text: Fantastic ladies — they're unreal!

indicators.note: fantastic means fanciful or wild, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An exclamation that some wonderful women seem too good to be true.
explanation.definitionFit: Perfect standards or models exist only in the mind and are never fully realised.

clue.text: Old German fish

definitions.meaning: a member of the Germanic tribe that settled in England with the Saxons
to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: An elderly German goes fishing, or an ancient German fish.
explanation.definitionFit: One word names both an early Germanic settler in Britain and the act of fishing with a hook.

clue.text: Able climber, say, mounting rugged rock right away

indicators.note: in a down entry, mounting reads the letters upwards, back to front

parts.note: e.g. means say, for example

indicators.note: rugged rock is broken and uneven, so the letters are rearranged
right is sent away, removed from rock

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A capable climber, for instance, scaling rough rock straight off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounting' turns EG into GE; 'right away' takes R from ROCK, leaving OCK, which 'rugged' rearranges to CKO.
explanation.definitionFit: A small lizard with adhesive toe pads, famous for scaling walls and ceilings.

clue.text: English learner interrupting scripture put on curfew and sent down

indicators.note: the English learner breaks into scripture, sitting inside it

parts.note: RE is religious education, scripture lessons at school
L is the learner driver's plate
a student who is gated is confined to college as punishment

explanation.surface: A student of English disrupts a scripture class, is confined and then expelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent down' suggests expulsion from university but means demoted, like a football team dropping a division.
explanation.definitionFit: A demoted football team has been moved down a division, banished to a lower league.

clue.text: Drain central heating after fish turns up

indicators.note: the heating abbreviation comes after the fish
in a down entry, turning up reads the word backwards

parts.note: an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: Instructions to drain the heating system after a fish appears in it.
explanation.definitionFit: To bleed someone dry is to sap or exhaust their resources, as a bloodsucker does.

clue.text: Song about nasty man in nice place

indicators.note: the song goes around the nasty man

parts.note: an aria is an operatic song
a cad is a dishonourable man

explanation.surface: A song about a villain set in a pleasant spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastoral paradise of Greek legend, an idyllic rural region.

clue.text: Consider it realistic to conceal state

indicators.note: the words consider it realistic hold the state within them

explanation.surface: Someone thinks it plausible for a government to keep secrets.
explanation.definitionFit: An independent country in the Horn of Africa, a sovereign nation.

clue.text: Ancient listed hall has so crumbled

indicators.note: a crumbled building has fallen apart, so these letters are reassembled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A heritage-protected old hall has fallen into ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: A listed building in Britain is one legally protected for its historic value.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for very old, as aged as the landscape itself.
